Custom.SalesDescription.newValue:
Crew Scheduling on the Customer Service Order Planning Board

Adds crew-based scheduling to the Customer Service Order Planning Board, allowing schedulers to assign a predefined crew to a Customer Service Order in a single drag-and-drop action rather than selecting each technician individually.

A new setting under System Setup > Scheduling > Technician Trips ù Allow Scheduling Crews on Customer Service Order Planning Board ù controls the feature. When disabled, the Customer Service Order Planning Board behaves exactly as it does today. When enabled, the Technicians tab is relabeled Technicians/Crews and gains a toggle to switch between a Technicians view and a Crews view.

The Technicians view shows only technicians who are not members of any crew, removing the need to visually filter out already-assigned crew members. Technicians removed from all crews reappear in this list automatically. Scheduling an individual technician from this view works exactly as it does today.

In Crews view, each crew card displays the crew name, member count, and utilization. Dragging a crew onto a Customer Service Order opens the scheduling modal with a Crew Assignment tab, where the dragged crew is pre-selected and all of its members are pre-checked. Schedulers can add support technicians outside the crew via a secondary popup, search within the member list, and deselect any individual technician for that specific assignment. Changes made in this modal apply only to the trip being created ù the crew's default membership is not modified, and defaults reset fresh for each subsequent assignment.

Before the assignment is confirmed, each selected technician is checked for an overlapping scheduled trip or blocked time using the same conflict-detection logic as the Technician Planner. If any conflict is found, the entire assignment is blocked and a notification identifies each conflicting technician by name. No partial scheduling of the remaining technicians occurs.

Crews can be created and edited directly within the Customer Service Order Planning Board. A New Crew button above the Crews list opens a popup where a crew name and at least one technician must be specified before the crew can be saved. Each crew card includes an edit icon that reopens the same form with existing values pre-populated, enabling crew name and membership changes at any time.

When the feature setting is enabled, the Crew Planner trip tile editor also exposes a technician multi-select showing all technicians currently included in the crew trip, allowing per-trip membership to be adjusted after initial scheduling. If all original crew members are removed from a trip, the crew association is cleared and the trip is no longer linked to a crew record.

Custom.ResolutionNotes.newValue:
What was changed

Crew scheduling was added to the Service Order planner, and the crew planner side was aligned with it. A new System Setup checkbox ("Allow Scheduling Crews on CSO PB") turns the whole feature on or off. When it is on, the Service Order planner panel gets a Technicians/Crews switch with a crew list, buttons to create and edit crews, and crews can be dragged onto a Service Order to schedule them. The scheduling popup that opens for a crew includes a Crew Assignment tab, and it blocks the whole assignment if any selected technician already has an overlapping trip or blocked time. Crew records can now be created and edited from the planner board, where before they could only be displayed. When every original crew member is removed from a trip, the trip is now converted to individual technician trips correctly, both when creating a trip and when editing one.

Dragging a crew onto a Service Order
Crews can be dragged from the planner panel onto a Service Order, and individual technicians can still be dragged the same way. When an item is dropped, the board looks at what type of item was dragged, so a crew always opens the crew scheduling popup and a technician always opens the technician popup. This matters because a crew and a technician can carry the same recorded number, so the form is chosen by item type rather than by that number. The crew that was dragged is already selected in the popup. The popup shows everything the technician scheduling popup shows, plus a Crew Assignment tab containing: the crew selector, a "+ Support Techs" button that opens a popup for picking technicians from outside the selected crew (the ones added appear in the list under the crew members), a search box that filters both lists as it is typed, and the crew's members already ticked. When a trip is being edited, the ticks reflect the technicians already on that trip. Changing the ticks here only affects the trip being scheduled ù the crew record itself is never changed from this popup.

Overlap validation for the whole crew
While the crew assignment popup is open, every selected technician is checked for an overlapping trip or blocked time in the chosen period. The check runs about half a second after editing stops, so it does not fire on every keystroke. If any selected technician has an overlap, their row is flagged with the "Overlapping" chip and every Save button is disabled, so it is not possible to schedule only the technicians who have no conflicts. If a save is attempted anyway (for example after a change made elsewhere), the server repeats the same check and refuses the whole assignment, showing a single error popup that lists each conflicting technician, the message that the technician "is unable to be scheduled to this Service Order due to an overlapping scheduled trip/blocked time", and that technician's overlapping events; the popup has no confirm button. When nothing conflicts, the crew is scheduled as one trip per selected technician, all linked to the same crew and the same crew trip.

Create / edit crews
A new popup lets crews be created and edited from the planner. It contains the crew name, a search box with a result count, a list of technicians with tick boxes (and a "No technicians found" message when the search matches nobody), a Cancel button and a primary button that reads "New Crew" when creating and "Edit (crew name)" when editing. Creating stays disabled until a name and at least one technician are given; editing starts with the crew's current members ticked and stays disabled until the name or the selected technicians change. Both close on a successful save, show a loading spinner while saving, and re-enable the form if the save fails. Saving a crew is new on the server side: the name and all members are validated first (a name is required, at least one technician, no duplicates, every selected person must be an active technician, and all members must share at least one common primary service zone) and are then written in one operation, so a failure cannot leave a half-saved crew. The earlier approach, which created the members one at a time and deactivated them again on failures, was removed. After a successful save the crew list refreshes automatically.

Crew planner trip tile edit
The same crew assignment popup is used on the crew planner. The Crew Assignment tab appears when the System Setup switch is on and the trip is new or has not started yet, and it lists the technicians already on that crew trip ù after this change that list can differ from the crew's current members, which is expected.
Edge case ù all original crew members removed
If every original crew member is unticked: when creating a trip, the crew field clears itself (and its error message disappears), and the trip is created as individual technician trips for the technicians still ticked, without any crew link. When editing a trip, saving removes the crew from that trip, so its technician trips become individual trips for the same technicians and times, with the edited start time and duration applied. The same save also creates individual trips for any technician who was newly added to the trip and did not already have one on that crew.
